# A body without a usable vanId is refused, with two different messages

**Claim.** A well-formed object that simply has no vanId is refused differently from a body that is not an object at all, so the message distinguishes 'you forgot the id' from 'I could not read this'.

Applies to: `~1people~1{vanId}~1mergeInto/put`

## Observed exchange

```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Priya",
  "lastName": "Raman-{scope}"
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```

_A JSON object that parses fine but names no counterpart._

```http
PUT /people/100000001/mergeInto

{}

→ 400
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "INVALID_PARAMETER",
      "text": "Must specify VanIDs for merging"
    }
  ]
}
```

_A body that is valid JSON but not an object at all._

```http
PUT /people/100000001/mergeInto

"nope"

→ 400
{
  "errors": [
    {
      "code": "INVALID_PARAMETER",
      "text": "The body of the request is null or cannot be parsed."
    }
  ]
}
```
